Decimal literals such as Decimal("1E-7") and Decimal("1E+3") currently raise ValueError while building an expression. Parse the coefficient and exponent exactly, and normalize representable negative scales to zero so both typed filters and predicate.to_sql() queries preserve the value. Checked arithmetic bounds the Decimal128 coefficient to 38 digits, preserves existing scale limits, and rejects nonfinite or overflowing values. This does not add Decimal256 literal support.

Added 21 cases covering actual Arrow-backed table queries, SQL queries, zero, signed exponents, precision boundaries, and errors. Both Python 3.11 and 3.13 expression suites pass 123 tests; the baseline fails 10 of the new cases. Python binding Rust tests pass 13; official make doctest passes 77 with 6 skips; Ruff, Rustfmt, hooks, Pyright and workspace/tests/all-features Clippy with -D warnings pass. A fresh environment restored from the original dependency freeze passes the full required suite: 1528 passed, 37 skipped, 68 deselected (143.51s); while optional Torch suites have the same baseline remote mock-server ordering failure.

Tested against f4544628; observed official main d864e719 contains one Catalog API commit without expr or Cargo.lock changes. AI assistance: gpt-6.1-sol assisted implementation and local validation; all reported checks were actually executed.
